profile.description: GCP Axion c4a, 32 Neoverse-V2 cores, PocketTTS English streaming. C96 is the qualified operating point, measured on the shipped default with nothing exported. Host-scoped: this is not a generic Arm profile and makes no claim about a 16-core host or about Magpie.

hardware.smt_policy: OFF; one thread per physical core
hardware.notes: GCP c4a, no SMT. The load generator ran on the same box for every number here, which costs ~13% coalesced client reads: the cadence percentiles are upper bounds on server lateness, not the server's true emission.

requirements.blas: BLAS=none is the Linux default and the only setting these numbers describe. A codec measurement taken under Accelerate puts the phases in a different order and is not comparable.
requirements.isa: ASIMDDP for the int8 codec kernels

server.why: 16x2 beats 8x4 decisively here: at equal threads and equal slots, RTF p95 0.784 against 1.052, throughput -25%, stall@250 84/17968 against 734/13511. The optimum is a property of the model's T_frame(B) = a + b*B ratio, not of the machine -- qwen-tts at 1.7B prefers 4x8 on this same host. max_batch is capped at 16 by MYNAH_GRAPH_MAX_JOBS and is not binding at C90 (about 6 live slots per worker).

MYNAH_QUANT_GROUPS.why: Must be ABSENT. quant_groups above is exactly POCKET_QG_DEFAULT_SPEC_PINNED since 2026-09-19, so a run that exports this variable is measuring a shell line rather than the product -- which is precisely the gap that went unnoticed for six days. An export also refuses the run rather than passing quietly.

MYNAH_PREFILL_SLICE.why: Must be ABSENT. The shipped default is 32 tokens per slice; setting it to 0 restores the one-shot prefill that froze the whole batch on every admission.

MYNAH_PREFILL_STEP_MS.why: Must be ABSENT. The shipped default is 60 ms of prefill work per AR step. This cap is what makes zero stalls a scheduler bound instead of a lucky distribution; 0 removes it.

client_contract.why: At the operating point the worst client prebuffer measured 228.9 ms and max_gap never exceeded 142.8 ms against an 80 ms frame, so the 250 ms contract is covered by the sample maximum as well as by the bound. MYNAH_PREFILL_STEP_MS caps the prefill work one AR step may absorb at the measured slack, which is what makes it a bound rather than a statistic.

qualification.workload: Mixed v2 bank, streaming route /v1/audio/speech, PCM, one language pack, load generator on the same host.

ceiling.why_not_promoted: Thirteen stalls in ten minutes, while the TTFA gate still passed by half a millisecond. Measured at the OLD 60 ms prefill cap and not re-measured at 30, which is the change that promoted C96 -- so this is a stale ceiling and the first level to re-screen.

Both preferred gates fail: TTFA p95 522.6 and 22 stalls in ten minutes. RTF p95 0.817 means the box still has a fifth of a realtime budget in hand at a level it cannot qualify -- capacity is not what stops us here, continuity is. Measured at the OLD 60 ms prefill cap.

history.why_not_promoted: Before the prefill was sliced, admitting a request froze every resident slot: worst freeze 707 ms against an 80 ms frame. No level on the mixed bank could be promoted at all.

qualification.notes: The operating point moved C90 -> C96 on 2026-09-19 by setting the per-step prefill cap to the measured slack: T_frame(B) = 3.0 + 7.8*B ms puts a typical step at B6 at 50 ms of an 80 ms frame, leaving 30. Before that change C94 and C96 were both MARGINAL over thirty minutes by exactly one stall, in 53980 and 54186 requests. This is also the first point measured on a plain binary -- codec_convtr:int8 became the shipped default the same day, so nothing is exported. CAUTION for whoever reads the ceiling: C98 and C100 were measured at the old cap and are stale. A second caution about the instrument: TTFA p95 sits at 492 +/- 5 against a 500 ms gate, so a ten-minute verdict at these levels is a coin toss -- the same configuration returned MARGINAL and GOOD in two ten-minute runs separated by 136 microseconds of percentile.
